lessons: Open with a concise, surprising fact or vivid contrast – videos with hooks like “older than the United States” or “red meat vs white” keep >1.0 of viewers past 10% and >0.5 past 50%.
Limit the first 10‑15 % to the hook; replace detailed explanations with visual cues – biggest drops cluster at 0.1‑0.15 and are all explanatory lines.
Use concrete, visual language (e.g., “shark roams Arctic depths”, “tuna looks like deep‑red beef”) – these correlate with kept_at_50pct > 0.6 and kept_at_end > 0.4.
Avoid generic or repetitive statements in the early segment – low‑retention videos repeat facts like “dead skin cells would swell” and fall to ≤0.2 by 50%.
A countdown flag does not improve retention; videos with countdown = true perform no better than those without.
worst_moment_types: Early detailed scientific explanation without visual hook
Repetition of a known fact or definition
Generic “pause and guess” prompts lacking concrete imagery
best_hook_types: Vivid visual contrast between two familiar things
Short mystery/question that challenges a common belief
